**The meaning of the verses**
﴿وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾

… We raise the rank of whom We will in this world above others, as We raised the rank of Yusuf. And above everyone who has knowledge there is someone more knowing than him, until knowledge ends with Allah the Exalted, the Knower of the unseen and the seen.

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِّن قَوْمٍ عَسَىٰ أَن يَكُونُوا خَيْرًا مِّنْهُمْ﴾

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law: let no believing people mock other believing people; perhaps those who are mocked are better than those who mock, …

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. What did Sami say about Jawad when he first saw him? And what did Jawad know that Sami did not?
2. Why did Sami fall into the water? And what did Jawad do when he fell? Did he laugh at him?
3. Does the verse mean that a person should not be happy with what he knows? (No; knowledge is a blessing to be happy about and to thank Allah for, but no one should be looked down on because of it, and we listen to those who know what we do not.)

**This week's exercise**
Every day your child learns one thing from someone they think knows less than they do: their younger brother or sister, their grandmother, or a worker in the neighbourhood. At dinner they tell you what they learned, and from whom.
